findings.claim: In the host validation regex, the (\/.*)? path group is dead because before_validation strips everything from the first '/' before validation runs.

The plural *_ids hydration branch in Store._hydrateEmbedded always deletes *_ids keys, even when no sub-collection was side-loaded. This leaves arrays of undefined and breaks plain ID-list attributes such as muted_category_ids.

Store._hydrateEmbedded drops IDs for embedded relationships when the side-loaded data uses a different root key, for example featured_user_badges with root :user_badges. This produces arrays of undefined.

The migration indexes execute(...)[0]['id'] for the embed_category lookup without checking for an empty result. It raises IndexError when no matching site_settings row exists, such as on fresh installs or the test DB.
The uncategorized_category_id lookup at line 15 of the migration uses the same unguarded [0] index on the query result and fails on a fresh database.
The file (the serializer) ends with an extra trailing blank line, which breaks CONTRIBUTING's no-trailing-blank-lines rule.
In rest.js.es6, type.replace('_', '-') replaces only the first underscore, so a type containing several underscores resolves to the wrong base path.
embeddable_hosts.category_id is NOT NULL but has no foreign key, no existence check in the controller, and no dependent handling. Deleting a category leaves orphaned host rows.
The migration backfill interpolates legacy host strings directly into raw SQL (VALUES ('#{h}', ...)) without quoting or parameter binding. A value containing a single quote aborts the migration.
EmbeddableHost's before_validation calls self.host.sub! without a nil guard. A missing host raises NoMethodError (500) instead of producing a validation error.
A missing params[:embeddable_host] raises an exception in the controller instead of returning a validation error.

After saving an embeddable host, the client sets host.category from the possibly-null local categoryId instead of the category_id returned by the server. The server defaults that value to uncategorized, so the UI shows a blank category until reload.
Admin::EmbeddingController#update persists nothing and only re-renders show. The PUT customize/embedding route and the client saveChanges action that back it are therefore dead.
The new create/update/destroy and embedding show endpoints have no behavioural tests. The specs only assert subclassing of AdminController.
Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#update and #destroy use EmbeddableHost.where(id:).first and then call methods on the result. An unknown id raises NoMethodError (500) instead of returning 404.
The spec 'is false if embeddable_host is blank' no longer tests hosts, because Topic#expandable_first_post? dropped the host-presence check.
The contents of spec/fabricators/category_fabricator.rb and embeddable_host_fabricator.rb are swapped.
Host validation accepts a port (e.g. example.com:8080), but record_for_host compares against uri.host, which excludes the port. Such stored hosts never match.
The pretender GET /fruits/:id handler ignores the id and always returns fruits[0]. The store.find('fruit', 2) test therefore checks the wrong record and passes accidentally.
The migration uses def change with raw execute data moves and deletes the old settings. Rollback raises IrreversibleMigration and the old data cannot be recovered.
The admin.embedding.edit locale key is never referenced.
A spec context description contains the typo 'emeddable' instead of 'embeddable'.
The migration copies legacy host strings verbatim via raw SQL and bypasses the model's scheme/path normalization. Entries like 'http://eviltrout.com' never match record_for_host after the upgrade.
Icon-only d-button elements (save, cancel, edit, delete) have no accessible labels or title attributes, and the needed i18n keys do not exist.
record_for_host lowercases the host column with lower(host) but does not downcase the input host. Mixed-case hosts such as http://EvilTrout.com/x fail to match.
The serializer defines explicit id/host/category_id methods that only return object.<attr>, which duplicates what the attributes declaration already does.
The code uses hash-rocket syntax ':with =>', which goes against CONTRIBUTING's Ruby 1.9 hash syntax rule.
The inner 'if records.present?' check is redundant after val.present? and split.
Trailing \r and whitespace from the textarea are kept when legacy hosts are inserted in the migration.
In store.js.es6, obj[k].map throws TypeError when a *_ids field is null or not an array.
destroyRecord() has no .catch(popupAjaxError), so delete errors are swallowed.
The Embedding wrapper (OpenStruct with id 'default', plus its own controller, serializer, adapter and routes) and the plural _ids store hydration exist only to wrap a host list.
The Fabricator(:private_category) after_build uses update!, which persists even under Fabricate.build. It also calls transients[:group].id, which raises if no group is passed.
The host validation regex's [a-z]{2,5} TLD rule rejects localhost, IP addresses and TLDs longer than 5 characters such as .museum. Migrated rows that skipped validation then fail on later edit.

Feed-polled topics now take their category from the item's host record instead of the removed embed_category setting. Items from unregistered hosts get a nil category, and admins can no longer set the feed import category.
Spec files contain extra blank lines that violate RuboCop Layout/EmptyLinesAroundBlockBody.
The singleton embedding record is fetched with store.find without an id, which resolves to a collection.
In obj[pluralize(subType)] = hydrated || [], the || [] is dead code because map always returns an array.
The migration's create_table uses force: true, which drops an existing table on re-run.
before_filter :ensure_logged_in, :ensure_staff duplicates filters already declared by the parent Admin::AdminController.
There is no unique index or uniqueness validation on host. With duplicate hosts, record_for_host's .first picks a category arbitrarily.
